Entropy bonuses

A policy gradient learner can become certain before it has seen enough, as in Lesson 80. Adding a bonus $\beta H(\pi)$ for the policy's entropy pays it to stay uncertain. A small $\beta$ buys exploration; a large one stops the policy committing at all.

The maths

The entropy of a policy in state $s$ is

$$H\big(\pi(\cdot \mid s)\big) = -\sum_a \pi(a \mid s)\log \pi(a \mid s), \qquad 0 \le H \le \log|\mathcal{A}|$$

It is 0 for a deterministic policy and $\log|\mathcal{A}|$ for the uniform one. By Lesson 81, $H = \log|\mathcal{A}| - D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\pi \,\|\, \text{uniform})$, so a bonus on entropy is a pull towards uniform.

PPO adds it to the clipped objective with a weight $c_2$ (Schulman et al. 2017, eq. 9), alongside a value-function loss with weight $c_1$:

$$L_t^{\text{CLIP}+\text{VF}+S}(\theta) = \hat{\mathbb{E}}_t\Big[L_t^{\text{CLIP}}(\theta) - c_1 L_t^{\text{VF}}(\theta) + c_2\, H\big(\pi_\theta(\cdot \mid s_t)\big)\Big]$$

The paper writes the entropy term as $S[\pi_\theta](s_t)$. This page calls its weight $\beta$.

The gradient for a softmax policy. With $\partial \pi_a / \partial \theta_b = \pi_a(\mathbb{1}_{a=b} - \pi_b)$ and $\sum_a \pi_a = 1$,

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{\partial H}{\partial \theta_b} &= -\sum_a \frac{\partial \pi_a}{\partial \theta_b}\big(\log \pi_a + 1\big) = -\pi_b(\log\pi_b + 1) + \pi_b \sum_a \pi_a(\log\pi_a + 1) \\ &= -\pi_b\big(\log \pi_b + H\big) \end{aligned}$$

Actions more likely than typical ($\log\pi_b > -H$) are pushed down and rarer ones pushed up. The learners above add $\alpha\beta\,\partial H / \partial\theta_b$ to each gradient bandit update.

The exact target. Maximise $\sum_a \pi(a) q(a) + \beta H(\pi)$ subject to $\sum_a \pi(a) = 1$. With a multiplier $\lambda$, setting the derivative in $\pi(a)$ to zero gives

$$q(a) - \beta\big(\log \pi(a) + 1\big) + \lambda = 0 \quad\Rightarrow\quad \pi_\beta(a) = \frac{e^{q(a)/\beta}}{\sum_b e^{q(b)/\beta}}$$

The bonus turns "pick the best" into the softmax of Lesson 13 with temperature $\beta$. As $\beta \to 0$ it becomes greedy; as $\beta \to \infty$, uniform. Lesson 88 uses the same calculation with a KL penalty in place of entropy.
